deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. The page has two parts. The upright part holds tables of the linear forms (residue classes mod 4|D|) of primes p for which ±D is a quadratic residue, for D = 22, 23, 26, 29; a row for 30 is begun and left blank. This continues the residue tables of the previous page (quadratic residues mod 47 to 64). The upside-down part holds (a) a Latin statement headed 'Propositio quae Demonstrationem exspectat' (a proposition that awaits proof), (b) square roots of -3 modulo primes p ≡ 1 (mod 6), (c) power and index computations modulo 79, and (d) scattered scratch arithmetic.

A. TABLES. Gauss's sign labels are explained by the data. The row marked '+' is a one-sided list 4Dn + r. It is exactly the set of classes with (-D/p) = +1, so '+' corresponds to the form x^2 + D y^2. The row marked '-' is a symmetric list 4Dn ± r. It is the set with (+D/p) = +1, corresponding to x^2 - D y^2. Symmetry is forced: the character (D/.) is even for D > 0 and odd for -D < 0. In modern terms each row is the kernel of the Kronecker character mod 4D (or mod 2·23, 2·29 when D is odd), computed by quadratic reciprocity.

- 22, '+' row: the classes of p mod 88 with (-22/p) = (2/p)(p/11) = 1. Gauss gives 1, 9, 13, (15, 21 inserted), 19, 23, 25, 29, 31, (35, 43 inserted after a cancellation), 47, 49, 51, 61, 71, 81, 83. That is 19 classes. The correct set has 20: the same list plus 85.
- 22, '-' row: 88n ± {1, 3, 7, 9, 13, 21, 25, 27, 29, 39}, the 20 classes with (22/p) = 1. This row is correct and complete.
- 23, '+' row: 46n + {1, 3, 9, 13, 25, 27, 29, 31, 35, 39, 41}. These are the odd lifts of the quadratic residues mod 23 (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 13, 16, 18), i.e. (-23/p) = (p/23) = 1. Correct and complete; a cancelled tail follows.
- 23, '-' row: 92n ± {1, 7, 9, 11, 13, (15, 23 inserted), 25, 29, 41, 43}. The condition is (23/p) = (-1)^((p-1)/2) (p/23) = 1. The correct 11 values are 1, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 19, 25, 29, 41, 43. So the inserted '23' should be 19.
- 26, '+' row: 104n + {1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 15, 17, 21, 25, 27, 31, 35, 37, 43, 45, 47, 49, 51, 63, 71, 75, 81, 85, 93}. The condition is (-26/p) = (-2/p)(p/13) = 1. All 24 entries are correct and complete (37 and 63 are overwritten).
- 26, '-' row: 104n ± {1, 5, 9, 11, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25, 37, 39, 45, 49}. The condition is (26/p) = (2/p)(p/13) = 1. The correct 12 values are the same list without 39, which is divisible by 13.
- 29, '+' row: 116n + {1, 3, 5, 9, 11, 13, 15, 19, 25, 27, 31, 33, 39, 43, 45, 47, 49, 53, 55, 57, 65, 75, 79, 81, 93, 95, 99, 109}. The condition is (-29/p) = (-1/p)(p/29) = 1. All 28 entries are correct and complete.
- 29, '-' row: 58n ± {1, 5, 7, 9, 13, 23, 25}. These are the odd quadratic residues of 29 below 29. Correct and complete.

B. THE PROPOSITION (upside down). Reading, with the letters uncertain: 'Si datur Quadratum, quod per p divisum residuum r efficit — dabitur idem Quadratum quod per 4r+p [MS glyph read '4r+2' by the transcriber] divisum det idem residuum; siquidem 4r+p sit numerus primus.' In English: if some square leaves residue r on division by the prime p, some square also leaves residue r on division by 4r + p, provided 4r + p is prime.

The tables above use modulus 4D, which supports my reading of 'p' over '2'. On that reading this is Euler's form of quadratic reciprocity: (r/p) depends only on p mod 4r (the case p' = p + 4r). Gauss labels it explicitly as conjectural, 'awaiting proof'. This matches his own account of finding the theorem by induction in 1795 and proving it on 8 April 1796 (Tagebuch no. 2).

C. SQUARE ROOTS OF -3 (upside down). For p = 7, 13, 19, 31, 37, 43, 61 Gauss lists a, p-a, p+a, 2p-a:
- 7: 2, 5, 9, 12
- 13: 6, 7, 19, 20
- 19: 4, 15, 23, 34
- 31: 11, 20, 42, 51
- 37: 16, 21, 53, 58
- 43: 13, 30, 56, 73
- 61: 27, 34, 88, 95

In each case a^2 ≡ -3 (mod p). So these are all x < 2p with x^2 ≡ -3 (mod p); the odd ones satisfy x^2 + 3 ≡ 0 (mod 4p). Entries for 67 are missing. For 73 and 79 only scratch is written ('62×68', '17×11'). The true roots are 17 and 56 (mod 73) and 32 and 47 (mod 79) [my computation]. A further column (1, 4, 12, 21 / 3, 4, 28, 31 / 1, 12, 28, 61 / 4, 13, 57, 84 / 7, 12 / 4, 21) I could not identify.

D. COMPUTATIONS MOD 79. The column 50, 51, 22, 73, 16, 10 against 1 to 6 consists of the successive powers 50^k mod 79 (k = 1..6). The column 35, 40, 57, 20, 68, 10 consists of 35^k mod 79 (k = 1..6); the scratch '1400' is 40·35 and '1100' is 22·50. The third column 14, 28, 42, 56, 70, 6 equals 14k mod 78 (84 ≡ 6). Together with 35^14 ≡ 50 (mod 79) [my check], this shows Gauss building an index table (discrete logarithms) mod 79 with base 35: ind(50) = 14, ind(10) = 6. The remaining numbers (831, 1939, 102490, 320, 791, 1993 + 25, ...) are unexplained scratch.
errors: 22 '+' row (-22 residue): the class 85 mod 88 is omitted. E.g. p = 173 ≡ 85 has (-22/173) = +1. Even with the inserted 15, 21, 35, 43 the list has only 19 of the 20 classes.
23 '-' row: the interlinear insertion reads '15.23', but 23 is impossible (divisible by 23). The missing class is 19 ((23/19) = (4/19) = 1). Either a slip by Gauss or a misreading of '19'.
26 '-' row: 39 is listed but is divisible by 13 and must be deleted. The correct list is ±{1, 5, 9, 11, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25, 37, 45, 49}.
Sign convention: the row labelled '+' gives the classes where -D (not +D) is a residue, i.e. the '+' refers to x^2 + D y^2. This is not an error, but it is easily misread.
The -3 root table breaks off at 67; the entries at 73 and 79 are scratch products, not roots.

results.usually_credited_to: Euler (tables of divisors of quadratic forms, 1744-1783), Lagrange, Legendre

results.what: Conjecture: if r is a QR mod prime p, then r is a QR mod the prime 4r + p (stated as 'awaiting proof')

results.usually_credited_to: Euler (conjectured 1744/1783), Legendre (1785, incomplete proof), Gauss (first proof 1796)

deep.surprise_reason: The tables are routine Euler/Legendre-type material, with a few slips. The interesting item is an explicit 'Propositio quae demonstrationem exspectat' stating reciprocity in Euler's form as a conjecture. That is a documentary witness to Gauss's 1795 inductive discovery before his 1796 proof, which is already well known from his own testimony. The index computations mod 79 are standard Disquisitiones-era work.

transcription_corrections: Row labels: the row marked '+' lists primes for which -D is a residue (form x^2 + D y^2); the '-' row lists those for which +D is a residue.
Row 22 '+': '15, 21' and '35, 43' are interlinear insertions (the latter replacing a cancelled group); the class 85 is absent in the MS.
Row 23 '-': the inserted '(15.23.)' probably reads or should read '15.19'.
Row 26 '+': '37' and '63' are overwritten corrections, not doubtful readings.

Upside-down proposition: '4r+2' is more likely '4r+p' (Gauss's p glyph). The first line probably reads 'per p divisum residuum r efficit'. The word struck after 'divisum' is a cancellation, likely 'eandem'.
The column '50 14 / 51 2 28 / 22 3 42 / 73 4 56 / 16 5 70 / 10 6 6' should be read as rows (50^k mod 79, k, 14k mod 78).
Line '61 27 34 88 95' completes the -3 root table; 19, 43 and 61 appear underlined in the MS.
